findings.claim: Edward’s middle-class education places him in an Oxbridge career and eventually on a local council.
findings.truth: Edward leaves for university in Liverpool and later becomes a local councillor; the fetched plot source gives no basis for ‘Oxbridge career’.

findings.claim: The West End musical version opened at the Phoenix Theatre in London in 1988.
findings.truth: The 1988 West End revival opened at the Albery Theatre, transferred to the Phoenix Theatre in 1991 and closed in 2012. An earlier West End run opened at the Lyric Theatre in 1983.

findings.claim: By 1981, unemployment in Liverpool had reached around 20%.
findings.truth: Fetched sources corroborate industrial decline and severe Merseyside unemployment, but do not substantiate this precise citywide 1981 rate or its denominator. Cite an ONS or local-series source, or remove the number.
findings.evidence: History of Liverpool, Wikipedia, line 128; 1981 Toxteth riots, Wikipedia, line 125.

findings.claim: Russell himself described the play as Brechtian in structure.
findings.truth: This author attribution needs a citable Russell or authorised source. Without one, present Brechtian influence as an interpretation rather than as Russell’s own description.
findings.evidence: Fetched Blood Brothers and Bertolt Brecht reference pages did not substantiate the attribution.

findings.claim: Each song interrupts the action to comment on it rather than advance it.
findings.truth: The fetched plot account ties songs such as ‘My Child’, ‘Bright New Day’ and ‘I’m Not Saying a Word’ to decisions and transitions. Revise the recurring absolute claim throughout the unit to say songs can comment on events and can also advance the plot; retain only song-specific claims that can be supported.
findings.ruling: Softened in the lesson that states it absolutely; other lessons' song-specific claims left.

findings.claim: Questions about practitioners are an AQA GCSE Drama question type.
findings.truth: The specification requires study of the set play and practical interpretation, but does not prescribe a named practitioner or a separate practitioner question. Brecht can be used as an interpretive lens, not presented as a question type.
findings.evidence: spec 3.1.1 (knowledge and understanding), 3.1.2 (set-play study), and 4.2.1.2 (Section B).

findings.claim: Russell himself described the play in Brechtian terms.
findings.truth: This author attribution needs a citable Russell or authorised source. Without one, present Brechtian influence as an interpretation rather than as Russell’s own description.
findings.evidence: Fetched Blood Brothers and Bertolt Brecht reference pages did not substantiate the attribution.

summary: Eight surgical edits correct verified production, plot and assessment claims. The wider claim that songs do not advance plot needs a unit-level revision; three source or statistic concerns are logged as notes.
